objective: Port netty-pkitesting 4.2.19.Final to Netty.NET.PkiTesting with the original names, structure, comments and tests, building and signing certificates with the BCL (CertificateRequest, System.Formats.Asn1, CertificateRevocationListBuilder, HttpListener) where the Java module uses Bouncy Castle and the JDK HTTP server.

ownerDecisions: Project, folder and assembly names are the namespace root of the module (owner decision 2026-11-19, see docs/codec-base-porting.md): each codec module takes the namespace of its main package, and the tests use <project>.Tests like the other test projects.

Owner decisions 2026-11-19 for the codec modules that only need codec-base: one project per Maven module; codec-socks is Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Socks (its Maven and JPMS name) and holds the socks and socksx namespaces; haproxy is HAProxy (the casing of the Java types in that package); socksx, v4 and v5 are Socksx, V4 and V5.

Owner decisions 2026-11-24: pkitesting is ported on the BCL (part of the handler ssl design, docs/handler-ssl-design.md); the project is Netty.NET.PkiTesting (word casing; the package has no type to take the casing from).

statusMeaning.verified: Every declared original test is mapped to a C# test with the same name (case may differ) and passes.
statusMeaning.clr-adapted: Ported with the original names, structure and comments; every CLR difference is stated in a // CLR: comment and in this entry. For tests, some original methods are CLR-inapplicable with recorded evidence.
statusMeaning.deprecated-not-ported: @Deprecated Java unit (or a helper serving one) that is not ported; the deprecation facts, reason, replacement and every original comment/test are recorded.
statusMeaning.jvm-only-replaced: JVM-only metadata or documentation unit replaced by its recorded CLR counterpart.

notApplicable.sourceComment: The key generators for some algorithms, in some providers, don't support key gen initialization.
notApplicable.member: static KeyPairGenerator keyPairGenerator(String keyType, AlgorithmParameterSpec spec,
notApplicable.reason: The comment explains why KeyPairGenerator.initialize(spec, rng) may throw UnsupportedOperationException in some JCA providers; the BCL key factories have no initialize step and no providers. A JCA Provider selects the implementation of an algorithm among the installed providers; the BCL has no provider registry: each key type is created by its own static factory and signs with its own methods (ECDsa.SignData etc.), so no API takes a provider (owner decision 2026-11-16: JVM-only API families are replaced without facades).
notApplicable.clr: Algorithms.KeyPairGenerator(keyType, spec) returns the BCL factory of the key type, which takes the parameters directly (src/Netty.NET.PkiTesting/Algorithms.cs).

review.scope: Owner decision 2026-11-24: pkitesting is ported on the BCL; Bouncy Castle and the JCA providers are replaced by the BCL types named here. internal static class with oidForAlgorithmName (same switch, toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) as ToLowerInvariant, UnsupportedOperationException as NotSupportedException). keyPairGenerator(keyType, spec, rng, provider) is KeyPairGenerator(keyType, spec), a Func<object> over the BCL key factory of the key type (ECDsa.Create(ECCurve), RSA.Create(int), MLDsa/MLKem/SlhDsa.GenerateKey); NoSuchAlgorithmException is CryptographicException. The JCA Signature engine of signature(algorithmIdentifier, provider) has no BCL type, so its sign path is Sign(algorithmIdentifier, privateKey, data) and its verify path Verify(algorithmIdentifier, publicKey, data, signature): SHA*withECDSA is ECDsa.SignData with DSASignatureFormat.Rfc3279DerSequence (the DER signature of X.509), SHA*withRSA RSA PKCS #1 v1.5, ML-DSA-*/SLH-DSA-* the pure algorithms; a mismatched key is a CryptographicException (InvalidKeyException). The bouncyCastle() provider, DefaultProvider and the Provider parameters are not ported; the two comments inside keyPairGenerator document provider behaviour and are recorded as JVM-only. The Java key objects (PublicKey, PrivateKey, KeyPair) are the BCL key objects, typed object, because MLDsa, MLKem and SlhDsa derive from Object and not from AsymmetricAlgorithm (measured, and the MLDsa page lists Object as its base class), so the owner's AsymmetricAlgorithm mapping cannot hold every key; a key pair without a private key (new KeyPair(publicKey, null)) is the BCL PublicKey, which has a constructor for every key type. The class also holds the CLR counterparts of the JCA accessors the BCL types lack, each with a CLR comment: GetPublic/GetPrivate (KeyPair), GetEncoded (PrivateKey.getEncoded, PKCS #8; a null private key throws NullReferenceException as Java dereferences it), CopyWithPrivateKey (a KeyStore key entry), GetSigAlgName (X509Certificate.getSigAlgName, the OID mapped back through oidForAlgorithmName), GetSerialNumber, GetBasicConstraints, GetTBSCertificate, GetSignature and GetUniqueId (read from the DER certificate with AsnReader, RFC 5280 4.1), and SignatureHash (the digest of a SHA*with* name, SHA-256 for the names without one, because CertificateRequest and CertificateRevocationListBuilder require a named hash that Signed ignores). The experimental BCL PQC members (SYSLIB5006: PublicKey(MLDsa/MLKem/SlhDsa), the PQC PKCS #8 exports and CopyWithPrivateKey overloads, PublicKey.GetMLDsaPublicKey and the whole SlhDsa type) are used inside #pragma warning disable SYSLIB5006 regions with a comment; MLDsa/MLKem key generation, signing and IsSupported are not experimental.

review.scope: Owner decision 2026-11-24: pkitesting is ported on the BCL; Bouncy Castle and the JCA providers are replaced by the BCL types named here. V3TBSCertificateGenerator/ExtensionsGenerator and the Signed + CertificateFactory round trip are the BCL CertificateRequest: createCertBuilder builds a CertificateRequest(subject, PublicKey, HashAlgorithmName) (the PublicKey constructor accepts every BCL key type), addExtensions fills CertificateExtensions in the Java order, and CreateCertificate (tbsCertToBytes + generateCertificate) calls Create(issuerName, Signed, notBefore, notAfter, serialNumber), which encodes, signs and parses the certificate; the private key is not attached to the X509Certificate2 (the bundle keeps the key pair, as in Java), so CreateSelfSigned and its CopyWithPrivateKey, which fail for ML-DSA on this Windows host, are not used. Extensions: X509BasicConstraintsExtension (critical), X509KeyUsageExtension built from the Java BIT STRING bytes and padding through its (AsnEncodedData, bool) constructor, X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension over the OIDs in ordinal (TreeSet) order, X509SubjectAlternativeNameExtension over the GeneralNames SEQUENCE (critical when the subject is empty), the CRL distribution points as X509Extension 2.5.29.31 over DistributionPoint encodings (one from CertificateRevocationListBuilder.BuildCrlDistributionPointExtension per URI; the cRLIssuer form written with AsnWriter, which the BCL builder cannot express), and the custom extensions (octet string, UTF8String, IA5String, ACME identifier) as X509Extension over AsnWriter output. The ACME identifier keeps Java's extnValue content (the given bytes); RFC 8737 defines it as the DER OCTET STRING of the digest, so a caller passes that for a conforming extension (finding recorded in the doc). Type mappings: X500Principal is X500DistinguishedName, Instant DateTimeOffset, BigInteger System.Numerics.BigInteger? (null = random), OptionalInt int?, URI Uri, InetAddress IPAddress (getHostAddress is ToString), TreeSet<String> SortedSet<string>(Ordinal); requireNonNull is ObjectUtil.CheckNotNull (ArgumentNullException) and has no counterpart for the value types; IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException, IllegalArgumentException ArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException NotSupportedException. The random serial is 20 RandomNumberGenerator bytes with the top bit cleared ([0, 2^159 - 1] as new BigInteger(159, random)); Create takes the serial as unsigned bytes, so a negative serial (forbidden by RFC 5280 4.1.2.2) throws OverflowException. algorithm(Algorithm) is Algorithm_ (CS0102: a method cannot share the nested Algorithm class's name, as handler's Builder_()). preferredSignatureAlgorithm reads the BCL PublicKey: RSA key size, the bit length of the EC X coordinate (BigInteger.GetBitLength), GetDSAPublicKey, the OIDs of Ed25519/Ed448 (RFC 8410; the Bouncy Castle "EdDSA" name never occurs and its branch is kept), the ML-DSA parameter set name from MLDsa.Algorithm.Name, and the ML-KEM OIDs; the last message names the key OID. Algorithm, KeyUsage and ExtendedKeyUsage are sealed classes with static readonly constants (Base64Dialect pattern) with Name(), ToString() and Values() (JLS 8.9.3); their fields are internal where CertificateBuilder reads them (C# private is limited to the containing type). Algorithm's parameter specs are the BCL parameter objects: ECCurve.NamedCurves.nistP256/nistP384 for secp256r1/secp384r1 (RFC 5480), the RSA key size (RSA.Create uses exponent 65537 = F4, measured), and NamedParameterSpec returns the MLDsaAlgorithm/MLKemAlgorithm/SlhDsaAlgorithm of the name when MLDsa/MLKem/SlhDsa.IsSupported is true, else UNSUPPORTED_SPEC; Ed25519/Ed448 have no BCL type and are always UNSUPPORTED_SPEC, so isSupported() reports what the BCL can do on the running platform (this host: ML-DSA and ML-KEM yes, SLH-DSA, Ed25519, Ed448 no) and supportSigning() stays the property of the algorithm. generateKeyPair(SecureRandom) is GenerateKeyPair() without the random source; generateKeyPair(SecureRandom, Provider), provider(Provider), secureRandom(SecureRandom), the provider/random fields and SecureRandomHolder are not ported (their Javadocs are recorded as JVM-only). BuilderCallback is an internal delegate over the extension collection (functional interface; internal because the package-private field holds it). The empty GeneralName/DistributionPoint arrays are not needed, because the names are byte[] encodings. The Java key objects (PublicKey, PrivateKey, KeyPair) are the BCL key objects, typed object, because MLDsa, MLKem and SlhDsa derive from Object and not from AsymmetricAlgorithm (measured, and the MLDsa page lists Object as its base class), so the owner's AsymmetricAlgorithm mapping cannot hold every key; a key pair without a private key (new KeyPair(publicKey, null)) is the BCL PublicKey, which has a constructor for every key type. The experimental BCL PQC members (SYSLIB5006: PublicKey(MLDsa/MLKem/SlhDsa), the PQC PKCS #8 exports and CopyWithPrivateKey overloads, PublicKey.GetMLDsaPublicKey and the whole SlhDsa type) are used inside #pragma warning disable SYSLIB5006 regions with a comment; MLDsa/MLKem key generation, signing and IsSupported are not experimental.

Owner decision 2026-11-24: pkitesting is ported on the BCL; Bouncy Castle and the JCA providers are replaced by the BCL types named here. The TBSCertList that Java assembles with Bouncy Castle (and RevocationServer signs with Signed) is built and signed in one call by CertificateRevocationListBuilder.Build(issuerName, X509SignatureGenerator, crlNumber, nextUpdate, hashAlgorithm, authorityKeyIdentifier, thisUpdate), so getEncoded takes the Signed generator and returns the signed CRL; the comment "Version 2" is kept above the builder call, which writes version v2. Differences of the BCL encoding (all within RFC 5280 5.1): nextUpdate is always written (RFC 5280 5.1.2.5: "Conforming CRL issuers MUST include the nextUpdate field in all CRLs"), so the constructor takes a DateTimeOffset, not a nullable one; revokedCertificates is omitted when empty (Java writes an empty SEQUENCE); the CRL Number (thisUpdate in Unix milliseconds, monotonically increasing as RFC 5280 5.2.3 requires) and the Authority Key Identifier (issuer name and serial number of the issuer certificate, because the builder writes no Subject Key Identifier) are added. The signature algorithm is the issuer certificate's, as cert.getSigAlgOID(), through Signed(X509Bundle). Instant is DateTimeOffset and Map.Entry<BigInteger, Instant> is KeyValuePair<BigInteger, DateTimeOffset>; the serial is written as its two's complement big-endian bytes (the DER INTEGER content).

Owner decision 2026-11-24: pkitesting is ported on the BCL; Bouncy Castle and the JCA providers are replaced by the BCL types named here. The BCL has no GeneralName type, so each method returns the DER encoding (byte[]) of one GeneralName, which CertificateBuilder joins into a GeneralNames SEQUENCE in the order the names were added. SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder encodes dNSName, rfc822Name, uniformResourceIdentifier and iPAddress (one name per builder; the GeneralName is read back from the built extension with AsnReader); it has no method for directory names, registered IDs or other names on .NET 10 (measured: AddDnsName, AddEmailAddress, AddIpAddress, AddUri, AddUserPrincipalName), so AsnWriter writes otherName ([0] IMPLICIT SEQUENCE { OID, [0] EXPLICIT value }), directoryName ([4] EXPLICIT Name) and registeredID ([8] IMPLICIT OID) as Bouncy Castle does. dnsName keeps URI.create("ip://" + name).getHost() as new Uri("ip://" + name).Host, which lower-cases the host and rejects a host java.net.URI would treat as registry-based (a wildcard) with UriFormatException. uriName(String) throws UriFormatException for URISyntaxException; AddUri writes the escaped absolute URI (measured: "ex ample/sän" is written as ex%20ample/s%C3%A4n), as toASCIIString(). ipAddress keeps the NetUtil validation (Common) and parses the octets with NetUtil.CreateByteArrayFromIpAddressString. The Bouncy Castle IOException/UncheckedIOException wrapping has no counterpart; AsnWriter reports an invalid encoded value as ArgumentException.

This must be done before CRLs can be served for that issuer, and before any of its certificates can be revoked. @param issuer The issuer to register. @param provider The {@code Provider} to use (or {@code null} to fallback to default)

A JCA Provider selects the implementation of an algorithm among the installed providers; the BCL has no provider registry: each key type is created by its own static factory and signs with its own methods (ECDsa.SignData etc.), so no API takes a provider (owner decision 2026-11-16: JVM-only API families are replaced without facades).

review.scope: Owner decision 2026-11-24: pkitesting is ported on the BCL; Bouncy Castle and the JCA providers are replaced by the BCL types named here. com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer is System.Net.HttpListener with the prefixes http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ and http://localhost:<port>/ (a listener on both starts without administrator rights on this host); a prefix needs an explicit port, so the random port of HttpServer.create(loopback:0) is taken from a loopback TcpListener bound to port 0, and the listener starts in the constructor (as HttpServer.create binds), retrying when the port was taken in between. The createContext("/") handler is a delegate field run by one dispatch loop (GetContextAsync), so requests are handled one at a time as by HttpServer's default executor; a handler exception aborts the response, as HttpServer closes the exchange. start() runs the loop on the thread pool: Java starts the server from a ForkJoin thread so that its dispatcher inherits daemon status, while .NET thread-pool threads are background threads that do not keep the process alive and new threads do not inherit the state, so the isDaemon() branch has no counterpart (comments kept). sendResponseHeaders(404/405, 0) (chunked) are responses without a body. getInstance keeps the double-checked locking with a private lock object (synchronized on the class); AtomicInteger is Interlocked.Increment; ConcurrentHashMap is ConcurrentDictionary; register takes a lock because GetOrAdd's value factory "may be called multiple times" where computeIfAbsent runs it once. The issuers map is keyed by the SHA-256 hash of the certificate encoding (Certificate.equals compares encodings, X509Certificate.Equals issuer and serial). nextUpdate: the Windows chain engine reported OfflineRevocation/RevocationStatusUnknown for a CRL whose nextUpdate equals thisUpdate (measured), so the CRL is valid for ten seconds; revoked certificates are then reported Revoked and expired CRLs are fetched again (measured), and the @implNote is kept with a CLR comment. register(X509Bundle, Provider) and the CrlInfo provider are not ported (JVM-only Provider); revoke uses Algorithms.GetSerialNumber; IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException and IllegalArgumentException ArgumentException; URI is Uri, Instant DateTimeOffset; CrlInfo's fields are internal (C# private is limited to the containing type).

Owner decision 2026-11-24: pkitesting is ported on the BCL; Bouncy Castle and the JCA providers are replaced by the BCL types named here. Java signs a DER to-be-signed structure and wraps it as SEQUENCE { tbs, AlgorithmIdentifier, BIT STRING }; in the BCL that wrapping is done by CertificateRequest.Create and CertificateRevocationListBuilder.Build, which take an X509SignatureGenerator ("Base class for building encoded signatures as needed for X.509 certificates"). Signed is therefore that generator: SignData(data) signs with Algorithms.Sign under the Java algorithm name, GetSignatureAlgorithmIdentifier writes the Java AlgorithmIdentifier SEQUENCE { OID } without parameters (oidForAlgorithmName), and BuildPublicKey returns the key's PublicKey. The builders pass the to-be-signed bytes, so the toBeSigned constructor argument and getEncoded(Provider)/toInputStream(Provider) have no counterpart; Signed(byte[], X509Bundle) is Signed(X509Bundle), taking the issuer certificate's algorithm name (getSigAlgName, Algorithms.GetSigAlgName) and the key pair's private key. requireNonNull is ObjectUtil.CheckNotNull.

notApplicable.sourceComment: Get the root certificate as a new {@link TrustAnchor} object. Note that {@link TrustAnchor} instance have object identity, so if this method is called twice, the two trust anchors will not be equal to each other. @return A new {@link TrustAnchor} instance containing the root certificate.
notApplicable.reason: java.security.cert.TrustAnchor is the PKIX trust anchor type of the JCA CertPath API; the BCL has no trust anchor type: X509ChainPolicy.CustomTrustStore holds the anchor certificates and the chain engine reads their name constraints extension itself.

review.scope: Owner decision 2026-11-24: pkitesting is ported on the BCL; Bouncy Castle and the JCA providers are replaced by the BCL types named here. X509Certificate is X509Certificate2 and the KeyPair the BCL key object (object; a PublicKey when the bundle has no private key). Certificates are compared by RawData (Certificate.equals compares encodings, X509Certificate.Equals issuer and serial), names by their DER encoding (X500DistinguishedName has no equality; CertificateRequest copies the issuer name bytes), and Arrays.copyOf is a range; Arrays.asList is the array as IList<T>. isCertificateAuthority uses Algorithms.GetBasicConstraints and isSelfSigned compares the unique identifiers read by Algorithms.GetUniqueId. getPrivateKeyPEM exports PKCS #8 with Algorithms.GetEncoded (a bundle without a private key throws NullReferenceException, the NullPointerException of Java). The MIME encoder (64-character lines, CRLF) is a Func<byte[], string> over Convert.ToBase64String. JSSE/JCA conversions are ported with their SslStream-ready BCL counterparts: toTrustManagerFactory() is an X509ChainPolicy with the root in CustomTrustStore, CustomRootTrust and RevocationMode NoCheck (a TrustManagerFactory initialized from a KeyStore disables revocation checking, while Online is the X509ChainPolicy default) - the type of SslClientAuthenticationOptions/SslServerAuthenticationOptions.CertificateChainPolicy; toTrustManager() is an X509Chain with that policy (Build is checkClientTrusted/checkServerTrusted); toKeyStore(char[]) is the PKCS #12 encoding (X509Certificate2Collection.Export with keyEntryPassword) of the root and, with a private key, the leaf carrying its key plus the intermediates; toKeyManagerFactory() is the SslStreamCertificateContext of the leaf loaded back from that PKCS #12 with the intermediates, offline: the Windows SslStream server rejects the ephemeral CopyWithPrivateKey key ("Authentication failed because the platform does not support ephemeral keys"), while a TLS 1.3 handshake with ToKeyManagerFactory() and ToTrustManagerFactory() succeeds (both measured in scratch probes on this host); the loaded PKCS #12 entries stay alive with the returned context (ConditionalWeakTable, 2026-11-24), because a self-signed bundle stores its certificate twice, both entries share one key container, and finalizing the unused entry deleted the key (SEC_E_UNKNOWN_CREDENTIALS, measured by the handler ssl tests). File is FileInfo: the temporary files are created with a random name between the Java prefix and suffix and deleted on AppDomain.ProcessExit (deleteOnExit); ISO_8859_1 is Encoding.Latin1. Not ported (comments recorded as JVM-only): getTrustAnchor() (TrustAnchor; the root certificate in X509ChainPolicy.CustomTrustStore is the anchor), toTrustManagerFactory(String) and toKeyManagerFactory(String) (JCA factory algorithm names), toKeyStore(String, char[]) (JCA key store types) and toTempKeyStoreFile(char[], char[]) (a key entry password separate from the store password, which X509Certificate2Collection.Export cannot write). On this Windows host the BCL cannot attach an ML-DSA (CNG import "The parameter is incorrect") or ML-KEM (PlatformNotSupportedException) private key to a certificate, so ToKeyStore/ToKeyManagerFactory fail for such bundles (measured).

generateKeyPair(RNG, new BouncyCastleProvider()) chooses a JCA provider; the BCL has none to choose, so the four algorithms generate their keys with the platform implementation and the same null checks.

@EnabledForJreRange(min = JAVA_24) is Assert.SkipUnless(ML-KEM and ML-DSA supported on this platform); IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException, IllegalArgumentException ArgumentException, hasMessageContaining Assert.Contains. Runs on this host.

@EnabledForJreRange(max = JAVA_11) runs the test only where the JVM has no EdDSA; Assert.SkipWhen(algorithm.IsSupported()) runs it while the BCL has none (always on .NET 10). Without a provider to pass, the builder rejects ed25519/ed448 with NotSupportedException when the algorithm is set, so the builder is created inside Assert.Throws, where Java expects NoSuchAlgorithmException from buildIssuedBy.

getSubjectAlternativeNames() is GetSubjectAlternativeNames, which decodes the extension with AsnReader into Java's [type, value] lists (RFC 2253 directory name, dotted IPv4, DER OtherName plus its OID and value); it decodes as Java 19+, so the pre-19 branch has no counterpart (its comment is kept). Negative Java byte literals are unchecked byte casts.

hasUnsupportedCriticalExtension() is the absence of X509ChainStatusFlags.HasNotSupportedCriticalExtension, getKeyUsage() the nine bits of the X509KeyUsageExtension, checkValidity() a range check, getNotBefore().getTime() the Unix milliseconds of NotBefore (local time).

providers() keeps only the default (null) row: the BouncyCastleJsseProvider row and register(root, provider) have no BCL counterpart, so Register(root) is used and the unused parameter is allowed with an xUnit1026 pragma and reason. The CRL is fetched by the Windows chain engine from the HttpListener RevocationServer.
As the valid case; the CertificateException "Certificate has been revoked" is the CryptographicException of CheckClientTrusted naming X509ChainStatusFlags.Revoked.

keyPair.getPublic() is the PublicKey from Algorithms.GetPublic, kept by the test because each call makes a new PublicKey; getPrivate() is Algorithms.GetPrivate (null), and the NullPointerException of getPrivateKeyPEM() is NullReferenceException.
The key pair is one BCL key object, so getPublic()/getPrivate() identity is Assert.Same on it and on Algorithms.GetPrivate.
toTrustManager() is the X509Chain of ToTrustManager(); checkClientTrusted(path, "UNKNOWN") is CheckClientTrusted; the Windows chain engine finds the path through the old issuer.
